g1.label: 1. By 17 December we ___ the survey to all 200 students, so the results will be ready after the break.
g1.why: By + a deadline takes the future perfect: the sending is finished by then.

g2.label: 2. Please don't call on Monday morning: I ___ the volunteers from nine until twelve.
g2.why: The future continuous describes an action in progress at a future time.

g3.label: 3. The signs are already up and the rules are agreed, so we are well ___ track.
g3.why: The fixed phrase is on track: making the expected progress.

g4.label: 4. The final report is ___ on 31 January, so we need a first draft before the exams.
g4.why: Due on a date means it must be handed in by then.

g5.label: 5. The booths took two weeks longer than planned. We are now behind ___, so something has to go.
g5.why: Behind schedule means later than planned; a calendar or agenda is not a plan's timing.

g6.label: 6. You have too much to do. Why don't you ___ the poster design to one of the volunteers?
g6.why: Delegate a task to someone means give them the work and responsibility.

g7.label: 7. By the time the campus reopens on 12 January, we ___ for the noise data for almost a month.
g7.why: By the time + a duration up to a future point needs the future perfect continuous.

g8.label: 8. The library staff are a key ___: nothing changes in the reading room unless they agree.
g8.why: A stakeholder is a person or group affected by the project.

g9.label: 9. The report is the main ___ of the pilot: it is the one thing we have promised to hand over.
g9.why: A deliverable is a finished piece of work you promised to hand over.

g10.label: 10. The booths cost ___ more than all the other milestones together.
g10.why: Far is a modifier before more; very cannot modify a comparative.
